text:
maya (support): FYI customer reported streaming disconnects on hosted API. Partial SSE chunks then the connection is closed from our side. Logs show write errors and an abort after ~30s of stalled writes.

maya (support): Logs:
```
[2026-03-17T14:00:12Z] stream: conn=abc123 writev: EPIPE
[2026-03-17T14:00:12Z] stream: conn=abc123 aborting stream after 30s stalled writes (queued=524288 bytes)
[2026-03-17T14:00:12Z] request=RQ-98765 model=gpt-x status=aborted reason=slow_consumer
```

maya (support): Customer says client was backgrounded on mobile and only reading intermittently. They also reported duplicate billing events when reconnecting quickly.

arjun (eng-runtime): Can you paste the exact request/curl and the client repro steps? Is this only for SSE endpoint or also chunked generation?

maya (support): Only SSE so far. request id RQ-98765. Repro curl: 
```
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \\n  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-x&stream=true'
```

maya (support): Python slow-reader repro:
```
python - <<'PY'
import requests, time
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-x&stream=true'
r = requests.get(url, stream=True, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REDACTED'})
for i, chunk in enumerate(r.iter_content(chunk_size=1)):
    time.sleep(0.6)  # slow consumer
    if not chunk:
        break
    print(i, chunk[:10])
PY
```

lucy (eng-sre): That log looks like our per-connection backpressure/abort path. Runtime soft-limit is 512KB queued per connection, then we start aborting after X seconds to avoid memory buildup. Why did queue get that big? Is net send buffer full?

arjun (eng-runtime): Runtime intentionally stops accepting more application-level buffers once we hit the waterline, but we should be yielding to kernel sndbuf. Can you grab net stats for conn=abc123? @infra-bot any tcp info?

infra-bot: netstat snapshot for conn abc123: tx_queue=0 bytes 328192, sndbuf=212992, rcvbuf=87380. socket write backlog in userspace ~524288.

arjun (eng-runtime): Hmm sndbuf smaller than our queued data -> kernel wasn't able to flush due to client not reading. We maintain app-level queue (512KB) + kernel queue; when both fill and no progress for 30s we hit abort. That explains writev/EPIPE when client disconnected.

maya (support): Customer also said they reconnected immediately and saw two invoice events for the same logical request (they had reconnect loop). Billing flagged it.

sam (billing): We see duplicate usage events for RQ-98765 when reconnect_count > 0 within 5s. We'll add a short dedupe window but recommend avoiding reconnect storms from clients.

arjun (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigations for customer: 1) add client heartbeat/ping to keep socket active; 2) read in a separate thread and drop app-level sleeps; 3) on mobile, register background handler to close stream when backgrounded. Also increasing client TCP sndbuf can help.

lucy (eng-sre): Longer-term: expose per-connection buffer and idle timeouts as config for Private/Dedicated, and for Hosted experiment increasing soft-limit to 1MB for a subset to measure impact. Filing internal ticket RNW-9876 to track runtime change + observability to surface queued bytes per conn.

arjun (eng-runtime): Repro notes for engineers: reproduce locally with slow-reader script above. Also simulate with `socat` or `nc` and a slow reader to see kernel sndbuf behavior. Example: `yes "data" | nc -l 8080` then connect with slow consumer.

maya (support): Customer accepted workaround (heartbeat + small client reconnect backoff). They're ok to wait for RNW-9876.

arjun (eng-runtime): Action items: (1) increase hosted soft-limit to 1MB for 1h canary (ops), (2) expose tuning docs for customers, (3) eng-runtime to implement safer abort path that emits final SSE event before closing.

lucy (eng-sre): Also add alert when a single conn's queued bytes > 512KB for >20s.

maya (support): Thanks all — will share repro and next steps with customer. :thumbsup: :eyes:
